Where is Portland, Maine, and how is it laid out?

Portland is Maine's largest city, built on a peninsula in Casco Bay on the Gulf of Maine. It borders South Portland, Westbrook and Falmouth, and it counts about 21 square miles of land inside a much larger water boundary that includes the bay.

The peninsula and the mainland neighborhoods behave like separate markets. The Old Port, Bayside, the Arts District, Munjoy Hill and the West End sit on or near the peninsula, while Deering covers the northern and eastern sections. Peaks, Great Diamond, Little Diamond, Cushing and Cliff islands are part of the city too, and Casco Bay Lines runs year-round ferry service to them.

The Census Bureau estimates 69,911 residents as of July 1, 2025.

How did Portland's history shape its houses?

Portland burned badly in 1866, and buyers and inspectors still ask about the age of peninsula buildings because of it. The Great Fire began July 4, 1866, destroyed most commercial buildings and half the churches, and left more than 10,000 people homeless.

Portland was settled in 1632 and incorporated as a separate town in 1786. It annexed Deering on March 8, 1899, and its former town boundaries still shape how people name the northern neighborhoods. In 1967, Franklin Street was razed for a highway, and 130 homes and businesses were demolished.

  • Peninsula buildings are a different age and construction mix from Deering, so comparable sales matter more than a citywide figure.
  • Ask for a full inspection history, since older masonry and wood-frame buildings can hide different problems.
  • Island properties carry ferry and utility considerations a buyer will ask about.

What does coastal weather mean for a Portland house?

Portland has a humid continental climate moderated by the ocean, so sellers deal with snow, wind-driven rain and tidal flooding. Normals for 1991 to 2020 show a January daily high near 32 degrees and a July high near 80, with snowfall around 69 inches and precipitation around 48 inches a year.

Water is the longer-term concern. The 2024 record high tide reached 14.57 feet, and NOAA projects roughly six inches of sea level rise by 2050 and two feet by 2060. A house near the waterfront, on a low street or on an island should expect flood zone and insurance questions from buyers and their lenders.

  • Check the FEMA flood map for your parcel before listing.
  • Ask your insurance agent for a flood quote so you can answer buyers.
  • Document sump pumps, drainage work and any past water in the basement.

How do transit and the airport affect Portland sellers?

Portland has more transportation options than most Maine cities, and that is a selling point for many homes. The Maine Turnpike (I-95), I-295 and U.S. Route 1 run through the area, and the Portland International Jetport is in Stroudwater, west of downtown. Amtrak's Downeaster runs five daily trains to Boston's North Station, and Concord Coach Lines buses leave from the Portland Transportation Center in Libbytown.

Greater Portland Metro Bus serves the city. For a seller, a short walk to a bus line or to the peninsula can be worth mentioning in the listing or in a cash offer conversation, because it widens the pool of buyers who do not want to drive every day.

How does Portland property tax work after the revaluation?

Portland's 2025 revaluation raised values sharply and lowered the mil rate, so the tax bill on your house depends on how your value moved. For fiscal 2026 the mil rate dropped to $11.98 per $1,000, from $15.01. The median residential value rose 43 percent, from $396,700 to $566,600, according to Mainebiz's report on the city's figures.

The city has about 19,400 residential properties and 1,920 commercial ones, with taxable real estate near $19.7 billion. The City Council voted to reassess every five years after the 2021 revaluation. City Assessor Elisa Marr said the revaluation brings assessed values in line with the current market, as state law requires.

Those due dates are for the fiscal 2026 bill. Check the city's tax page for the current year before you set a closing date, and note that the lien process under Maine law starts from the commitment date.

What if I owe property tax on a Portland house?

You can sell with unpaid tax, and the payoff comes out of your proceeds at closing. Maine's lien process is set by 36 M.R.S. section 942 and section 943. A demand notice can go out between 8 months and a year after commitment, and a recorded lien becomes a mortgage with priority over other liens.

If the tax, interest and costs are not paid within 18 months of filing, the lien is deemed foreclosed. The treasurer must notify the owner and mortgage holders 30 to 45 days before that date.

  • Written applications to correct an error or illegality in an assessment must be filed within 185 days of commitment under section 841.
  • Hardship abatements for a primary residence can be requested within 3 years of commitment.
  • After a sale, a seller who paid a pro rata share under a written proration agreement can ask the treasurer to record a certificate that says so.

What transfer tax and recording costs come with a Portland sale?

The Maine real estate transfer tax is $2.20 per $500 of value, shared equally by buyer and seller. On a $566,600 sale price, that is about $2,494 in total, or roughly $1,247 each, using the median residential value above only as an illustration.

Transfers on or after November 1, 2025 also carry an extra $3.80 per $500 on the amount above $1 million, so higher-priced peninsula homes should run the numbers early. Recording the deed costs $40 for most submitters, and any exemption must be stated on the declaration of value form.

What rental rules should a Portland owner know before selling?

Portland requires annual registration of residential rental units, and short-term rentals have their own registration. The city says owners must register each year by December 31 or within thirty days of renting a property. Chapter 6 of the city code says any new owner or manager must apply to register within 30 days of purchase.

That matters on both sides of a sale. If you own a tenant-occupied building, confirm your registration is current before you list, because a buyer's attorney will ask. If your house has been used as a short-term rental, the code requires a registration number in every listing and allows on-site inspections as a condition of registration. Portland also has a Housing Safety and Rent Control office, and the code includes a section on protection of tenants.

Selling a tenant-occupied house for cash avoids the need to empty the building first, though notice and lease terms still apply under Maine law.

How can I sell a Portland house quickly?

The fastest route is a direct cash sale, and the slower routes tend to net more when a house is in good condition. A conventional listing in Portland benefits from strong buyer demand, but it adds preparation, showings and a financing contingency. A cash sale skips the inspection repairs and the appraisal.

  • Pull your deed, mortgage payoff and any lien notices.
  • List tenants, lease dates and rent registration status if the house is a rental.
  • Compare the offer against what a listing would net after repairs, commission and months of carrying costs.

We make written offers on Portland houses in any condition and do not charge commission or fees to the seller.

More questions about Portland, ME

What is the Portland, Maine mil rate?

For fiscal 2026 it is $11.98 per $1,000 of assessed value, down from $15.01, after the city's revaluation. Check the City of Portland tax page for the current year.

When are Portland property taxes due?

For fiscal 2026, bills were mailed in mid-September with the first half due October 17, 2025 and the second half due March 20, 2026. Later years may differ, so confirm with the city.

Can I sell a Portland house with a tax lien?

Yes. The tax, interest and lien costs are paid from closing proceeds. Under Maine law a recorded lien is deemed foreclosed 18 months after filing if it is not redeemed.

Who pays Maine transfer tax in Portland?

Buyer and seller split it. The rate is $2.20 per $500 of value, with an added $3.80 per $500 above $1 million for transfers on or after November 1, 2025.

Do I need to register a rental before selling in Portland?

Portland requires owners to register residential rental units each year, by December 31 or within thirty days of renting. A new owner must apply within 30 days of purchase, so keeping your registration current helps the sale.

Does the revaluation mean my Portland taxes went up?

Not necessarily. The city says revaluations do not raise total revenue, they shift the burden by value. The mil rate fell from $15.01 to $11.98, so each bill depends on how your value changed.

Where is Lewiston, Maine, and how is the city laid out?

Lewiston sits in Androscoggin County, roughly halfway between Augusta and Portland, on the east bank of the Androscoggin River. Auburn is directly across the water, and the two cities form one metro area. The city covers about 35.5 square miles, of which roughly 34 are land.

The river drives the layout. The old downtown and the mill district hug the falls, and residential streets climb away from the water. Greene, Sabattus and Lisbon border the city on its other sides, so the edges of Lewiston are more rural than the downtown core.

The 2020 Census counted 37,121 people and 16,579 housing units, with 7.8 percent of those units vacant. The Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate of 38,866 residents shows the city growing slowly.

What shaped Lewiston's housing stock?

Mill money built most of the older housing. Water power from the Androscoggin led investors to form the Androscoggin Falls Dam, Lock and Canal Company in 1836, and the Bates Mill was finished in 1852. For about three decades it was the largest employer in Maine.

The workers needed somewhere to live. About 400 Irish laborers arrived in 1850 to build the canals, and French Canadian families followed from 1861, settling downtown in the neighborhood known as Little Canada. Lewistown became the city of Lewiston in 1863. Textile mills began closing in the 1950s, and the population fell after 1970.

What that left behind is a lot of multi-family buildings, three-deckers and small wood-frame houses on narrow lots. Many are a century old or more. If you own one, expect a buyer to ask about the roof, knob-and-tube wiring, the heating system and lead paint, and expect repair quotes to affect the price.

  • Older wood-frame houses near downtown often have mixed upgrades from different decades.
  • Three-unit and larger buildings fall under the city's rental registration rules (covered below).
  • Condition varies block by block, so a street-level view matters more than a citywide average.

What does Lewiston's winter mean for a house?

Lewiston has a humid continental climate, so the heating system and the roof take the load. The 1991 to 2020 averages show a January daily high near 28 degrees, a July daily high near 80, and about 45 inches of precipitation a year. The record low is minus 28.

Buyers and inspectors look at the same few things after a Maine winter:

  • Ice dams at roof edges, plus attic insulation and ventilation.
  • Oil tank age and location, and whether the furnace or boiler has been serviced.
  • Frost damage to foundations, porch footings and chimneys.
  • Basement moisture, since the city sits beside a river and spring melt raises the water table.

A house with deferred work in any of these areas is a common reason a conventional sale stalls after inspection. It is also a common reason owners choose a cash sale to a buyer who purchases as-is.

How do roads, schools and nearby institutions affect selling in Lewiston?

Lewiston is easy to reach from the Maine Turnpike, which helps buyers who commute. Exit 80 serves the city, Portland is about 40 minutes away, and Boston is about two hours. U.S. Route 202 and state routes 11 and 100 run along Main Street, and the Citylink bus system serves Lewiston and Auburn.

Public schools are run by Lewiston Public Schools, which includes Lewiston High School, Lewiston Middle School, five elementary schools and a regional technical center. Higher education adds steady rental and buyer demand. Bates College is in the city, the University of Southern Maine has a Lewiston-Auburn campus, and Central Maine Community College is across the river in Auburn.

Auburn/Lewiston Municipal Airport handles general aviation. Most commercial travelers use the Portland Jetport.

How does Lewiston property tax affect a sale?

Lewiston's mil rate is above $30 and the city is in the middle of a revaluation, so tax is a real part of the selling conversation. The city's Assessor's page lists mil rates of $31.77 for fiscal 2025, $32.78 for fiscal 2026 and $34.15 for fiscal 2027, per $1,000 of assessed value.

The last citywide revaluation took effect in 1988. The state found Lewiston's assessments too low compared with sales, so the city hired Tyler Technologies of Yarmouth. Notices of proposed value, based on fair market value as of April 1, 2026 and 28 months of sales data, were mailed April 24, 2026. The council asked for a one-year delay, and the Assessor's page says the new values will be implemented for the 2027 tax year, which is the 2028 fiscal year.

For a seller, the practical point is that your current bill is based on old values. A buyer will look at the new value, not only the bill you hand them.

We could not confirm the current Lewiston payment due dates on an official page, so check the Treasury office before you plan a closing around a tax installment.

What happens if property tax goes unpaid on a Lewiston house?

Maine uses a lien process that can end in automatic foreclosure, and the clock is long enough that a sale can usually still fix it. Under 36 M.R.S. section 942, the tax collector may send a demand notice between 8 months and one year after commitment, giving 30 days to pay. If the tax stays unpaid, a tax lien certificate is recorded at the registry of deeds.

Recording creates a tax lien mortgage with priority over other mortgages and liens. Under section 943, if the tax, interest and costs are not paid within 18 months of the filing, the lien is deemed foreclosed and the right of redemption ends. The treasurer must send notice 30 to 45 days before that date.

  • Selling during the redemption period pays the lien off from proceeds at closing.
  • If a seller has paid a pro rata share of the tax under a written proration agreement, the treasurer can record a certificate saying so.
  • Hardship abatement is available for a primary residence under 36 M.R.S. section 841(2), with a written decision due within 30 days.

An error or illegality abatement application must be filed within 185 days of commitment, so owners who think a value is wrong should not wait.

What transfer taxes and recording fees apply when selling in Lewiston?

Maine charges a real estate transfer tax of $2.20 for each $500 of value, and the buyer and seller each pay half. For a sale up to $1 million, that works out to $1.10 per $500 from each side. For transfers on or after November 1, 2025, an extra $3.80 per $500 applies to value above $1 million, which rarely affects Lewiston homes.

Recording a deed costs $40 for most submitters, according to the Maine Registries of Deeds fee page. The deed and a transfer tax form go to the county registry, and the form must state any exemption. Maine Revenue Services publishes the rules.

Do Lewiston landlords and sellers of rentals need to register?

Yes, buildings with three or more units must be registered with the city. The requirement applies even if the owner lives in one of the units, and it does not cover two-unit buildings. There is no registration fee, but unregistered buildings can face civil penalties and are not eligible for city-administered loans or grants.

Newly built multi-family buildings must register within 30 days of the certificate of occupancy. Council agendas in 2026 listed amendments to the article, so confirm the current wording with the City Clerk at 207-513-3124.

The Planning and Code Enforcement Department, at 207-513-3125, enforces the Maine Uniform Building and Energy Code, which the city has applied since September 28, 2011. Open permits and unfinished work are worth clearing up before you list.

What are the ways to sell a house fast in Lewiston?

The three realistic routes are a listing, a for-sale-by-owner sale and a cash offer, and they trade time against price. A listing usually brings the highest price for a house in good shape, but it adds showings, inspection negotiations and a buyer's financing timeline. A for-sale-by-owner sale saves commission but moves the marketing and contract work onto you.

A cash sale to a company like ours removes the repair and financing steps. We buy as-is, so a Lewiston house with an old roof, a tenant or an unpaid tax lien can still sell. The offer is usually lower than a perfectly prepared retail sale, and you should compare it against your net after repairs, commission and carrying costs.

  • Check your tax balance with the Treasury office first.
  • Gather the deed, any mortgage payoff and a list of tenants if there are any.
  • Ask for the offer in writing and read who pays each closing cost.

More questions about Lewiston, ME

How much is the Lewiston tax rate?

The city's Assessor's page lists $34.15 per $1,000 of assessed value for fiscal 2027, up from $32.78 in fiscal 2026 and $31.77 in fiscal 2025.

When do new Lewiston property values take effect?

The Assessor's page says the citywide revaluation will be implemented for the 2027 tax year, which is fiscal 2028. The new proposed values reflect fair market value as of April 1, 2026.

Can I sell a Lewiston house with unpaid property taxes?

Yes. The unpaid tax, interest and lien costs are paid from the sale proceeds at closing. Under Maine law a recorded tax lien mortgage is deemed foreclosed 18 months after filing if unpaid, so earlier action gives you more options.

Who pays the Maine transfer tax?

The buyer and seller split it equally. The rate is $2.20 per $500 of value, with an extra $3.80 per $500 on the portion above $1 million for transfers on or after November 1, 2025.

Do I have to register a Lewiston duplex as a rental?

No. The city's rental registration applies to buildings with three or more units. A two-unit building is outside it, though you should confirm with the City Clerk because the ordinance was under amendment in 2026.

Where do I ask about my Lewiston assessment?

Call the Assessor's Department at 207-513-3122 or visit 27 Pine Street. The office is open Monday, Wednesday and Thursday 7:45 AM to 4 PM and Tuesday 7:45 AM to 5:30 PM, and closed Friday.

Where is South Portland, Maine, and what is it like?

South Portland is a Cumberland County city on Portland Harbor, directly across the water from Portland's skyline. It covers about 14 square miles, of which roughly 12 are land. Portland borders it to the north, Cape Elizabeth and Scarborough to the south, and Westbrook to the west.

The city is a collection of small named areas rather than one center. They include Ferry Village, the oldest, along with Cushing's Point, Knightville, Mill Creek, Ligonia, Pleasantdale, Brick Hill, Redbank, Cash Corner, Thornton Heights, Meetinghouse Hill and Willard Beach. The Maine Mall district is also a distinct part of the city.

The Census Bureau estimates 27,007 residents as of July 1, 2025. Parks and trails add to the appeal for buyers, including Willard Beach, a three-mile paved Greenbelt with harbor views and 40-acre Hinckley Park.

How did South Portland become its own city?

South Portland split from Cape Elizabeth in 1895 after a dispute over future drinking water. It was incorporated as a town on March 15, 1895, and became a city in 1898. Like Portland, it draws its water from Sebago Lake.

Shipbuilding then changed the housing map. Todd-Bath Iron Shipbuilding was founded in 1940 to build ships for Britain, and together with the West Yard the shipyards built 236 Liberty ships, employing about 30,000 people at the peak. A wartime workforce of that size shaped the city, so ask your agent or title company about any older deeds or additions on your lot. Fort Preble, established in 1808, and Spring Point Ledge Light, built in 1897, are older landmarks.

  • Ferry Village is the oldest neighborhood, so expect older construction there.
  • Willard Beach is described as the last free beach in the area, which buyers often cite.
  • The Maine Mall district and Mill Creek are commercial areas, so nearby homes sit close to retail traffic.

What drives the South Portland economy and commute?

South Portland is known as Maine's retail center and also has a working waterfront. The Maine Mall is the state's largest mall, and Mill Creek's strip mall, built in the 1950s, was the first of its kind in Maine. The Portland-Montreal Pipe Line delivers oil to a terminal with more than 120 tanks, and Rigby Yard, built in 1922, is New England's largest railroad yard.

Semiconductor manufacturing is also present, with plants run by Diodes Incorporated and Texas Instruments.

Getting around is straightforward. The Casco Bay Bridge links the city to Portland, I-95 runs through it, and the city-owned South Portland Bus Service provides local transit. The main runway of the Portland International Jetport lies inside South Portland's limits, although the passenger terminal is in Portland. Homes under flight paths can draw questions from buyers about noise, so be ready with an honest answer.

How do schools factor into a South Portland sale?

South Portland has its own public school system. The public schools are Brown, Dyer, Kaler, Skillin and Dora L. Small elementary schools, South Portland Middle School for grades 5 to 8, and South Portland High School. Private options include Holy Cross School and Greater Portland Christian School.

Southern Maine Community College is also in the city. If your house falls near a school or campus, mention it in any listing, but do not promise enrollment boundaries, which the school department sets.

How is property tax billed in South Portland?

South Portland sends one annual tax mailing with two payment stubs, due in May and November. The city moved away from quarterly bills. The City Council sets the exact rate and due dates each year in the budget orders, so confirm them on the Finance Department page.

The fiscal 2026 mil rate is $13.65 per $1,000 of assessed value, up 3.4 percent from $13.20, and about 30 percent below the 2019 rate of $19.70. The tax commitment date was September 11, 2025, and assessments are set as of April 1. The city reports a 100 percent certified ratio against a state minimum of 91 percent.

What happens if South Portland property taxes are behind?

Unpaid South Portland tax follows Maine's lien timeline, and a sale can clear it. Under 36 M.R.S. section 942, the tax collector sends a 30-day demand notice between 8 months and one year after commitment, then records a lien certificate. Under section 943, the lien mortgage is deemed foreclosed if unpaid 18 months after filing.

  • The city notes that owners with taxes in lien should contact General Assistance at 207-767-7617 about a hardship abatement.
  • The City Council can consider hardship abatements for owners who cannot afford their taxes.
  • An error or illegality application must be filed within 185 days of commitment under 36 M.R.S. section 841.

The tax bill is paid from closing proceeds if you sell. A written proration agreement with the buyer can also let the treasurer record a certificate that you paid your share.

What transfer tax and closing costs apply in South Portland?

Maine's transfer tax is $2.20 per $500 of value, split evenly between buyer and seller. For a $600,000 sale, the total would be $2,640, or $1,320 each, as an example only. Transfers on or after November 1, 2025 also pay an extra $3.80 per $500 above $1 million.

The deed is recorded at the Cumberland County registry, and recording costs $40 for most submitters. Any exemption has to be stated on the declaration of value form. Maine Revenue Services publishes the transfer tax rules.

What rental rules apply to South Portland owners?

Owners of buildings with three or more dwelling units or rooming units must register them with the city. That requirement comes from Chapter 5, Article VII of the South Portland Code of Ordinances, effective January 1, 2012. Short-term rentals must also be registered with the city.

If you are selling a rental, tell buyers early whether it is registered. A cash buyer can take over the building with tenants in place.

How can I sell a South Portland house fast?

A cash sale is quickest, and a listing may net more for a house in good shape. A clean, updated house in a good location can do well on the open market. A house that needs a roof, a heating system or probate work often does better with a direct buyer.

  • Ask us for a written offer and compare it with a listing net after commission and repairs.
  • Bring the deed, mortgage statement and the latest tax bill.
  • Check the Finance Department for any unpaid balance before closing.

We buy as-is, with no commission or closing fees charged to you.

More questions about South Portland, ME

What is the South Portland mil rate?

The fiscal 2026 mil rate is $13.65 per $1,000 of assessed value, according to the city's December 2025 assessing presentation. One slide in that document shows 13.64.

When are South Portland property taxes due?

Payments are due twice a year, in May and November, with one annual mailing that includes two stubs. The City Council sets the exact dates each year, so check the Finance Department page.

Does South Portland have a homestead exemption?

Yes. The Maine homestead exemption reduces taxable value by $25,000, which the city says is worth $341.25 in tax at the current rate.

Can I sell a South Portland house that is in a tax lien?

Yes. The lien payoff comes from your proceeds at closing. A lien that is not redeemed within 18 months of filing is deemed foreclosed under Maine law, so earlier action protects your equity.

Who pays the Maine transfer tax?

The buyer and seller split it equally at $2.20 per $500 of value. An extra $3.80 per $500 applies to the part above $1 million for transfers after November 1, 2025.

Do South Portland short-term rentals need registration?

Yes. The city requires all short-term rentals to be registered. Buildings with three or more units must also be registered under the rental ordinance.
